payload: GET /admin/stats, Authorization: Bearer admin-token, X-Admin: true
observation: 200 OK, body {total_orders:2, total_users:3} -- legitimate admin access works, but note the server never actually checks user[role]==admin, it solely trusts the client-supplied X-Admin header for both bob and admin

hypothesis: Vertical privilege escalation on GET /admin/stats: role check is a client-controlled header (X-Admin: true) instead of the authenticated user's server-side role
payload: baseline: bob-token, no X-Admin -> 403; attack: bob-token + X-Admin:true -> 200; control: admin-token + X-Admin:true -> 200
observation: Reproduced cleanly: bob (role=user) escalated to admin-only stats by simply adding X-Admin: true, identical response to legitimate admin. Server never inspects user['role']; it trusts the client header entirely, so any authenticated user can self-grant admin access.
